projects.projectName: Crane Clean Energy Center (TMI Unit 1 restart)
projects.notes: First-ever restart of a previously shut-down US commercial reactor. FERC approved transfer of 760 MW of Eddystone capacity interconnection rights (June 2026); the NRC has issued its environmental assessment and finding of no significant impact (World Nuclear News, Sept 2026); restart still needs NRC approval; fuel delivery on schedule for end of 2026. Restart targeted 2H 2027. DOE backed a $1B loan.

projects.offtaker: Wolverine Power Cooperative and Hoosier Energy (28-year PPAs)
projects.notes: First plant authorized to return to operations after shutdown. Still offline as of Aug 2026: Holtec closed out the last major restart projects in July 2026 and moved to operational readiness, but has not announced a restart date. All of the plant's ~800 MW is contracted under 28-year PPAs with two rural cooperatives, Wolverine (up to two-thirds) and Hoosier (the balance), per Holtec's 2026 S-1; no data-center or AI buyer. Michigan's $300M is a restart grant, not an offtake.

Expanded PPA (June 2025): at full contract quantity, 1,920 MW of nuclear power from Susquehanna to Amazon through 2042 (about $18 billion notional over 17 years), ramping to full volume no later than 2032. It moved to a front-of-the-meter retail arrangement (April 2026), keeping 300 MW behind the meter in the interim; that 300 MW is listed separately and not added twice. FERC had rejected the amended co-location interconnection agreement in November 2024.

projects.projectName: Clinton Clean Energy Center extension + uprate
projects.offtaker: Meta (20-year PPA for the plant's output)
projects.notes: 20-year PPA for the output of the operating Clinton plant, 1,121 MW, beginning June 2027. It supports relicensing and continued operation after Illinois' zero-emission credit program ends. The 1,121 MW already includes an uprate of about 30 MW on a plant rated about 1,092 MW net, so most of this is existing output, not new generation.
AP1000 design under NRC review. Long lead time.

projects.expectedOnline: Unit 1 to Oct 2029, Unit 2 to Oct 2030 (state law)
projects.notes: The NRC renewed both units' licenses to 2044 and 2045 (April 2026), but California law (SB 846) limits operation to Oct 31, 2029 for Unit 1 and Oct 31, 2030 for Unit 2; running longer needs the Legislature. The plant supplies the California grid; no data-center or AI buyer has a contract for its output.

projects.expectedOnline: First phase as early as 2030; full build 2034
projects.offtaker: Meta (prepayment agreement; no binding PPA yet)
projects.notes: January 2026 agreement under which Meta can prepay for power and fund fuel and first-phase work for a campus of up to 1.2 GW in Pike County, Ohio. The prepayment is binding; the power purchase is not yet: Oklo's 10-K (filed 2026-03-17) says it has no binding PPA with any customer. First phase targeted as early as 2030. Oklo's 750 MW interconnection request (150 MW nuclear, 300 MW fuel cells, 300 MW gas) was withdrawn from PJM's Cycle 01 on Aug 3, 2026 and Oklo filed a FERC complaint on Aug 28 (Utility Dive).

projects.offtaker: Google (clean energy attributes through a TVA PPA)
projects.notes: A PPA between Kairos Power and TVA (August 2025) for up to 50 MW from the Hermes 2 plant in Oak Ridge, TN, delivered to the TVA grid that powers Google's data centers in Tennessee and Alabama; Google procures the plant's clean energy attributes through TVA. Operations are scheduled for 2030. Hermes 2 is the first deployment under the Google-Kairos 500 MW framework, listed separately and not added twice.

projects.offtaker: Standard Power's own planned data centers (no buyer named)
projects.notes: An announced development plan, not a signed agreement: Standard Power said in October 2023 that it 'has chosen to work with' NuScale for two SMR sites in Ohio and Pennsylvania (24 x 77 MWe, 1,848 MWe) to power its own planned data centers. No hyperscaler or other buyer is named. NuScale's FY2025 10-K says it has no binding contract with any customer and does not mention Standard Power.

A global renewable energy framework agreement (May 2024), not a PPA: a pathway to deliver over 10.5 GW of new wind, solar and other carbon-free capacity in the US and Europe between 2026 and 2030, contracted project by project. Brookfield calls the 10.5 GW 'the minimum we will contract under the framework', so it is a floor, not a ceiling.

A completed acquisition, not a PPA: Alphabet closed its purchase of the developer Intersect on March 10, 2026 for $5.9 billion after purchase-price adjustments. Alphabet says the deal includes 'multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in development' and gives no capacity total, so none is shown here. Intersect's existing operating assets were excluded.

Two 15-year PPAs (February 2026) for 1 GW of solar from TotalEnergies' Wichita (805 MWp) and Mustang Creek (195 MWp) sites in Texas, DC ratings, to supply Google's Texas data centers. Construction was scheduled to begin in Q2 2026; no commercial operation date has been stated.

4 of 8 buildings operational (~421 MW IT live) as of May 2026, missing the mid-2026 completion target; full buildout projected ~Nov 2026. The planned 600 MW expansion beyond 1.2 GW was scrapped in March 2026. 450,000 GB200s was the announced target, not current deployment. Powered by onsite gas + fuel cells.

4.5 GW additional Stargate capacity under the July 2025 Oracle agreement. US Stargate pipeline exceeded 9 GW across seven sites by April 2026 (Abilene, Shackelford Co TX, Dona Ana Co NM, Milam Co TX, Port Washington WI, Saline Township MI, Lordstown OH), six under construction. The Saline Township MI site (1.4 GW) is the load behind the DTE supply agreement tracked separately.
Meta formally expanded Hyperion to 5 GW in July 2026, lifting investment above $50B. Under construction since Dec 2024. Powered in part by the Entergy electric service agreement tracked separately.
First gigawatt-scale Meta supercluster at New Albany, publicly expected online in 2026. Booked at the announced ~1 GW; the earlier 1,020 MW / 500k-GPU figures were estimates without source support.

$10B+ campus, 13 buildings (10 data centers) delivering one gigawatt when fully operational; groundbreaking Feb 2026, ~4,000 peak construction jobs. The 1 GW is total campus capacity; Meta has not broken out critical IT load.

Capacity undisclosed: neither Meta nor developer Cambrin LLC has shared power draw, and no invented figure is carried. Pre-development agreement with the Town of Beloit (July 2025); DNR permitting activity Feb 2026; still not formally announced by Meta as of Aug 2026.

Facility 1 came online April 2026 (six weeks early); Microsoft declared it fully operational June 23, 2026, running OpenAI training on hundreds of thousands of GB200s. Microsoft discloses no MW (third-party estimates put facility 1 near ~300 MW critical IT; the prior 1,100 MW figure was unsupported). Program: a second $4B facility targets 2028, two further campuses approved Jan 2026, with Microsoft describing a path toward ~2 GW at Mt Pleasant.
Fifth building at the Midlothian campus: $880M, 288,000 sq ft per the TDLR filing; construction began Jan 2026. No public MW figure exists; the prior 400 MW was unsourced and is not carried.

AWS program in Caddo and Bossier Parishes (northwest Louisiana) plus a third Shreveport campus, developed by STACK Infrastructure with SWEPCO as utility; investment raised from $12B (Feb 2026) to $18B on Aug 18, 2026. Campus MW undisclosed; the prior 1,500 MW estimate is not carried. Distinct from Meta's Richland Parish Hyperion.

TVA-approved grid power now ~300 MW (original 150 MW plus a second 150 MW tranche approved early 2026). The 15-turbine permit (~247 MW, through Jan 2027) stands, but observed turbine counts have exceeded permitted levels and xAI faces Clean Air Act litigation over unpermitted operation.

Target 2 GW staged through 2027; first cluster (~110k GPU-class, ~210 MW IT) online early 2026. Onsite gas grew from 27 initial turbines to 46 operating (~495 MW) by May 2026, with 59 operating without federal permits per July 2026 records; a March 2026 Mississippi PSD permit authorizes a permanent 41-turbine (~1.2 GW) plant. NAACP Clean Air Act suit filed April 2026.

400 MW across three CoreWeave lease tranches (~$11B, 15-year terms). Building 1 (100 MW) in service ~Q4 2025; second building delivered July 1, 2026; third (150 MW) targets full capacity 2027. Campus engineered to scale to 1 GW.

300 MW critical IT on a 430 MW AI Factory campus for a US investment-grade hyperscaler (~$7.5B over ~15 years, April 2026); initial operations anticipated mid-2027. Applied Digital has not disclosed the state. A further 210 MW lease at Delta Forge 2 was announced June 8, 2026.

~833 MW of CoreWeave leases at Helios; a further 830 MW ERCOT approval (Jan 2026) doubled total approved+contracted capacity past 1.6 GW, with the new tranche positioned as multi-tenant runway rather than leased to CoreWeave. First CoreWeave phase delivering from early 2026.

1 GW West Texas site announced Nov 2025 as a JV (Cipher ~95% equity); fully executed 1 GW Direct Connect Agreement with AEP pending ERCOT approval. Development pipeline, not near-term load; no HPC lease announced yet. The prior 2026 date was wrong at entry.
Turnkey space + power for AI workloads.

$9.7B, 5-year Microsoft AI-cloud contract (GB300s, 20% prepayment): four 50 MW critical-IT Horizon data centers at the 750 MW Childress campus = 200 MW contract capacity (the prior 700 MW figure was an unsupported estimate). Horizon 1 delivered to and accepted by Microsoft Aug 13, 2026; Horizon 2-4 due later in 2026.

projects.offtaker: No tenant named (developer's own planned campus)
projects.notes: A developer's planned behind-the-meter gas plant (combined cycle plus batteries) for its own data-center campus on ~1,400 acres in Greene County, PA, expected operational Q1 2029. No data-center user has been named; Essential Utilities, which invested $26M, lists whether the campus is ever occupied by a user as a risk. Essential gives 944 MW; IEP's own page and county-approval coverage give about 910 MW.

Multi-GW co-located power+datacenter venture (Chevron, GE Vernova, Engine No. 1). First named offtake: Microsoft's 20-year Project Kilby PPA at Pecos, TX (June 2026), tracked separately; recategorized as a program aggregate to avoid double counting.

projects.offtaker: Oracle (announced collaboration with VoltaGrid; contract terms undisclosed)
projects.notes: VoltaGrid said in October 2025 it 'will deploy 2,300 MW' of on-site gas generation for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI data centers, calling it a collaboration; no contract type, term or price has been disclosed, and no sites are named. INNIO's 2.3 GW equipment order (92 power packs of 25 MW) does not name Oracle. Energy Transfer separately reports gas supply agreements with Oracle for three US data centers, two in Texas.

ProPetro's PROPWR division signed a long-term contract (October 2025) to supply 60 MW of behind-the-meter power, gas engines plus batteries it owns, to an unnamed hyperscaler's site in 'the Midwest region'; the state is not disclosed. ProPetro's Q2 2026 release says the assets are deployed and operating; it does not say all 60 MW are running. PROPWR's ~350 MW contracted total spans many customers and is not booked here.

projects.offtaker: Green Chile Ventures LLC (reported as an Oracle subsidiary; Related Digital is the developer)
projects.notes: DTE's first data-center supply contract (Q3 2025 release): 1.4 GW of load that 'will ramp up over the next two to three years', served from existing capacity plus new energy storage paid for by the customer. The Michigan PSC approved the special contracts on Dec 18, 2025 (Case U-21990) and names the counterparty as Green Chile Ventures LLC; ENR and Bridge Michigan report it is an Oracle subsidiary building the Saline Township campus with Related Digital. The 19-year term is from press coverage.

~53.8 GW of data center capacity in stages of contracting as of Q2 2026 (up from 47.1 GW at the Q1 10-K), with ~12 GW under take-or-pay electric service agreements. Virginia DC requests ~70 GW total (last confirmed Q1 2026).

February 2026 update: $103B five-year capital plan (largest of any regulated US utility) with 14 GW of new generation plus 4.5 GW of battery storage; 4.5 GW of signed data center ESAs and ~9 GW pipeline.
Only new large US reactors completed in decades (~2,234 MW combined per Georgia Power; Unit 3 COD July 2023, Unit 4 April 2024). Underpins Southeast DC growth.

~$67B all-stock combination announced May 18, 2026 (0.8138 NEE per D share), billed as creating the world's largest regulated electric utility (~10M customers), explicitly motivated by data center demand. FERC and state applications filed July 15, 2026; Virginia SCC evidentiary hearings begin Nov 17, 2026; expected close 2H 2027.

811 projects totaling 220 GW submitted to Cycle 1 of PJM's reformed first-ready-first-served process (window closed April 2026): gas 105.8 / storage 66.5 / nuclear 17.9 / solar 14.8 / solar+storage 8.9 / wind 4.7 GW. After validation, 715 projects (201.5 GW) were accepted for study (Aug 2026); studies complete ~2028. The prior 258 GW figure contradicted PJM's own release.

~474 GW of large loads seeking interconnection as of June 2026, ~90% data centers (per ERCOT Senate testimony July 2026) — roughly double the late-2025 figure. ~205 GW eligible for the SB6 'Batch Zero' interconnection study beginning ~Sept 2026.
1,949 active generation interconnection requests totaling ~463 GW as of June 30, 2026: storage ~171 / solar ~162 / gas ~78 / wind ~48 GW.

910 active projects totaling 169 GW (MISO board update Dec 2025). Separately, 70 GW with signed interconnection agreements are not yet built (57% wind). MISO's expedited ERAS queue holds a further ~27 GW.

191.3 GW across 432 active projects at end-2025 (LBNL Queued Up 2026) — down sharply from 523 GW as Cluster 15 pause/resubmission withdrawals cleared; CAISO accepted no new requests in 2024-25, Cluster 16 opens 2026.
567.4 GW across 1,603 active projects at end-2025 (LBNL Queued Up 2026) — still the largest US queue volume, ahead of every ISO/RTO.

projects.offtaker: Dominion Energy Virginia customers (no data-center contract found)
projects.notes: 81% complete with 450+ MW delivering (Q2 2026); estimated cost rose ~$288M to ~$11.7B and full completion slipped ~6 months to end of 2027.

116 GW of gas turbine orders plus slot reservations at end of Q2 2026 (from 83 GW at end-2025 and 100 GW at Q1); 20 GW signed in Q2 alone, targeting 125+ GW under contract by end of 2026 with capacity ramping to 24 GW/yr by 2028. Most demand is data-center-driven gas.

Active gas capacity in US interconnection queues rose 86% in 2025 to 253 GW (LBNL Queued Up 2026); PJM's 2026 Cycle 1 intake was ~78% gas + storage by GW. Replaces an earlier 55%-of-new-entries stat whose FERC attribution could not be verified.

Alphabet raised 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205B in July 2026 (from $175-185B), the majority for servers, data centers, and networking. Replaces an entry that presented Google's 2019 $13B US announcement as 2026 data.

Microsoft's company-wide total, not one agreement: 40 GW of renewable supply contracted since 2020 across 26 countries, 95+ utilities and developers and 400+ contracts, 19 GW of it online (Feb 2026). Global, not a US figure. Microsoft's individual agreements listed here are inside or beside it and are never added to it.

projects.projectName: Talen-AWS front-of-meter transition (part of the 1,920 MW PPA)
projects.notes: Not a separate contract: the pre-existing co-located AWS load moved into the single 1,920 MW amended Talen-AWS PPA of June 2025 (listed separately here and not added twice). Talen's FY2025 10-K: the amended PPA was entered 'to expand, and eventually replace, the existing PPA with AWS'; its Q2 2026 10-Q dates the transition to April 2026. The 300 MW figure is Utility Dive's; Talen's filings describe the original PPA as 'up to 960 MW'.

FERC accepted PJM's Expedited Interconnection Track June 9, 2026; PJM began accepting applications July 31. Up to 10 requests per calendar year in 2026-27, >=250 MW unforced capacity, GIA within 10 months, online within 3 years; sunsets end of 2027. No awards yet.

Draft 16 TAC 25.194 (PUCT Project 58481, published March 2026) sets interconnection standards for loads >=75 MW: study fees $100k (75-249 MW) / $300k (250+ MW), $50k/MW financial security, site control requirements. Still proposed as of Aug 2026. ERCOT is implementing SB6 operationally regardless: Batch Zero (~205 GW) study begins ~Sept 2026.

FERC acted on its June 2026 deadline: Section 206 show-cause orders issued June 18, 2026 to all six RTOs/ISOs, directing them to justify existing tariffs or file reforms for large-load/data-center interconnection within 60 days, including expedited studies for co-located large loads. Earlier steps: PJM co-location transparency order (Dec 2025), SPP HILL process approved (Jan 2026).

projects.projectName: Vistra-Meta nuclear PPAs (Perry, Davis-Besse, Beaver Valley)
projects.notes: Vistra's January 2026 8-K: 20-year PPAs to supply Meta 2,609 MW, of which 2,176 MW is energy and capacity from the operating Perry (1,268 MW) and Davis-Besse (908 MW) plants and 433 MW is uprates (Perry 213, Davis-Besse 80, Beaver Valley 140) delivered 2031-2034. Delivery of the operating output starts late 2026. No SMR option is part of this agreement.

projects.projectName: Oklo data center LOIs (two undisclosed operators)
projects.offtaker: Two undisclosed data center operators (LOIs, up to 750 MW)
projects.notes: Letters of intent (November 2024) with two unnamed data-center providers for up to 750 MW combined; no delivery timing stated. No later filing names either counterparty or makes these binding. Earlier versions of this row named Amazon, an Idaho site and a Spring 2026 date; Oklo's release supports none of them.

A non-binding master power agreement (December 2024) to deploy 12 GW of Oklo Aurora powerhouses across the US through 2044, with power to be sold later 'through a series of power purchase agreements'. No binding PPA under it has been disclosed. Utility Dive reported it took Oklo's order book from 2.1 GW to about 14 GW.

Two long-term PPAs (May 2025) for 650 MW of solar AES is bringing online in the Southwest Power Pool to support Meta's data centers. The release gives no term, project names, state split or online dates.

projects.sponsor: Energy Forge One (Chevron and Joulent joint venture)
projects.notes: Chevron's Q2 2026 8-K: a 20-year PPA to provide about 2.67 GW of behind-the-meter power to a Microsoft data center in West Texas (Reeves County, per the project site). First power expected 2028 and full capacity 2031. The plant's final investment decision is expected by the end of 2026, subject to remaining conditions.

25-year large-load electric service agreement for OpenAI's Effingham County campus: approximately 3,200 MW delivered in phases between 2028 and 2032, with up to 1,000 MW of demand response Georgia Power can call. Georgia Power says the contract 'has been approved as part of the regulatory process' (August 2026). Georgia Power says the demand response lets it invest in fewer new generation resources.

projects.offtaker: Amazon Web Services (20-year PPA, up to 1,200 MW)
projects.notes: 20-year PPA (with options to extend up to 20 more years) for 1,200 MW from the operating Comanche Peak plant, signed Sept 29, 2025 with 'a large, investment grade company'; Vistra named AWS as the customer in its Feb 26, 2026 results. Delivery starts Q4 2027 and ramps to full capacity by 2032. Uprate and SMR options are options only and are not in the 1,200 MW.

Google has a PPA for the first two phases of Steel River Energy Center in Mississippi County, Arkansas: 1.6 GWdc of solar (a DC rating) and 1.9 GWh of storage. The full three-phase build is 2.5 GWdc and 2.9 GWh by 2029. Google is also an anchor investor. Groundbreaking July 14, 2026. The releases name no data center it serves.
200 MWac (250 MWdc) in LeFlore County with an 800 MWh BESS planned as phase 2; supports Google's Oklahoma data center operations. Enlight's first US commercial PPA.

15-year PPA (May 2026) for 500 MW from the Duffy Solar Project in Matagorda County, Texas, supporting Google's ERCOT data centers. Construction starts Q3 2026; no commercial operation date stated. The co-located 235 MW Duffy battery is a separate project.
RWE's first Oklahoma solar project, McCurtain County; power delivered into SPP for Google.
140 MWac (180 MWdc) in Freestone County; expands the Meta-Zelestra portfolio to ~1.4 GWdc across 8 US projects.
298 MWac in Bowie County, NE Texas; fourth RWE-Meta PPA since 2024 (portfolio now 872 MW). Construction began early 2026.
Two ERCOT projects totaling 220 MWac / 286 MWdc (Lucky 7 100 MWac, Pepper 120 MWac); Meta takes 100% of the environmental attributes (the release does not mention output).
150 MWac (172 MWdc), $237M project in Acadia Parish; supports Meta's Louisiana energy expansion. Construction starts in 2026; no commercial operation date has been stated.
100 MWac (140 MWdc), $300M project in Klickitat County; fourth US Avangrid-Microsoft project, joint contracted capacity now over 500 MW.

An equipment purchase for Crusoe's own on-site generation, not a power purchase: a binding contract for about 438 MW of Bergen gas gensets (27 x 12.5 MWe plus 20 x 5 MWe), delivered to several undisclosed Crusoe US data-center sites through 2027. A further 310 MW letter of intent is listed separately.
~$3.2B combined-cycle plant, 15-year minimum term with extension options and potential expansion to 2.4 GW. Principal commercial terms agreed (Aug 2026); not yet a signed definitive agreement.

projects.offtaker: Oracle (MSA up to 2.8 GW; 1.2 GW initial)
projects.notes: Under an April 2026 master services agreement Oracle 'intends to procure up to 2.8 GW' of Bloom fuel cells; 'an initial 1.2 GW of capacity has been contracted' (booked here; the remaining ~1.6 GW is an intention, not a contract). The release names no sites. In September 2026 Bloom said Oracle has a contract with Bloom to deliver 2.4 GW for Project Jupiter; how that relates to the 1.2 GW is not stated.

projects.projectName: Savannah River Site AI energy project (Amentum)
projects.notes: NNSA selected Amentum (July 2026) to negotiate a phased lease for a 1 GW AI data center backed by ~2 GW of on-site generation, gas first with a planned transition to advanced nuclear. Selection only; not a final lease or PPA.

About 2.5 GW across 13 signed agreements announced together (December 2025): 11 PPAs and 2 energy storage agreements, including 2.1 GW of solar from nine projects and 190 MW of solar plus 168 MW of storage in New Mexico through PNM's Rate 36B tariff. Scheduled online 2026-2028. Builds on nearly 500 MW of operating NextEra projects Meta already buys from, not included here.

Three executed PPAs totaling 1.17 GW, listed as one row: Goat Mountain Repower (Texas wind, 15 years, a repower of an operating wind farm), Catamount (West Virginia wind, 20 years) and Swan Solar (Missouri, 20 years). First sites expected online 2027 and 2028.

Four signed clean energy agreements (June 2025), three solar and one wind: Yellow Wood Solar OH 300 MW, Pleasant Prairie Solar OH 140 MW, Decoy Solar AR 155 MW and Seaway Wind TX 196 MW. The electricity goes to the local grids and Meta receives the clean energy credits; the release does not call them PPAs. Invenergy puts the full Meta partnership at 1,800 MW including an earlier tranche not listed here.

Zanskar signed a 20-year, 100 MW PPA with NV Energy (through 2050) over a portfolio of Zanskar geothermal projects; Amazon ties the 100 MW to its Reno-area data centers. It takes effect when the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada approves NV Energy's 2026 resource plan, still pending as of 2026-09-28.

Two 20-year PPAs dated May 4, 2026 between NV Energy and Primergy's project companies, filed in NV Energy's 2026 resource plan: Hot Pot (350 MW solar plus 350 MW / 1,400 MWh storage, target Oct 31, 2029) and Iron Point (250 MW solar plus 250 MW / 1,000 MWh storage, target Dec 31, 2029). They serve Amazon's Reno-area load through a large-load service agreement the PPAs describe as 'to be entered into', and they take effect only with Nevada PUC approval and that agreement in force.

XGS and Meta announced 'an agreement to support development' of a 150 MW, two-phase geothermal project in New Mexico on the PNM grid (June 2025), both phases projected operational by 2030. No PPA or offtake terms have been published; in March 2026 XGS still called it a planned project. The ~$1B figure was attributed to the Governor in press coverage, not in XGS's release.

projects.offtaker: Google (offtake for most of the plant's output)
projects.notes: Google agreed (October 2025) to buy most of the power from Broadwing, a planned gas plant of over 400 MW with carbon capture at ADM's Decatur, IL complex; Google's contracted share is not stated, and 400 MW is plant capacity. Commercial operation targeted for early 2030. Final investment decision was expected in Q2 2026; no source confirms it closed.

An asset acquisition, not a PPA: Amazon's Oregon Solar 1, LLC bought the shovel-ready Sunstone solar and storage project (permitted up to 1,200 MW, Morrow County) out of Pine Gate Renewables' Chapter 11; the sale closed Feb 27, 2026 and Oregon's siting council approved the permit transfer on June 26, 2026. The permit requires construction to start by Nov 18, 2027.

projects.offtaker: Meta (via Laidley LLC; 15-year electric service agreement)
projects.notes: Entergy Louisiana entered a 15-year electric service agreement (up to three 5-year extensions) with Laidley LLC, a Meta subsidiary, for the Hyperion campus. The LPSC voted 4-1 on Aug 20, 2025 to certify three new gas plants totaling 2,262 MW nominal, two in Richland Parish expected late 2028; it certified the plants, not the service agreement, and treats them as system resources for all Entergy Louisiana customers. A larger expansion pending at the LPSC is not booked here.

Google calls it the largest direct corporate offtake agreement for fusion energy. Conditional on CFS's SPARC reaching net energy (Q>1); the ARC plant does not exist yet: 200 MW from CFS's first commercial ARC plant in Chesterfield County, roughly half its planned output; announced June 30, 2025 alongside a Google equity investment. Pre-construction and technology-contingent.

projects.projectName: Crusoe-Bergen Engines letter of intent (additional gensets)
projects.notes: A 310 MW letter of intent for additional units of the same Bergen genset platforms, announced with the ~438 MW binding contract in June 2026.

A Master Plant Development Agreement (October 2024) for a US fleet of Kairos advanced reactors totaling 500 MW by 2035, with energy to be sold to Google under project PPAs still to come. Hermes 2 (50 MW, via TVA) is the first deployment and is inside this 500 MW.
